invented.quote: Every school day, shortly after the first bell, the line starts forming outside my office.
invented.why: The brief gives the total number of first-period visits last fall, not that a line forms outside the nurse's office every school day shortly after the first bell.

invented.quote: students who had fallen asleep at their desks and couldn't shake it off.
invented.why: The brief says 'kids falling asleep' as a reason for visits, not specifically that they had fallen asleep at their desks and couldn't shake it off.

invented.quote: By mid-morning, many of those same students are fine. They weren't sick. They were exhausted.
invented.why: The brief only gives visit counts for the first three periods and does not state that the same first-period students are fine by mid-morning or that their symptoms were exhaustion rather than illness.

invented.quote: During adolescence, the body's internal clock shifts later, and most teens can't fall asleep much before 11 p.m., however early they go to bed.
invented.why: The brief does not mention adolescent circadian rhythm shifts or a specific 11 p.m. threshold before which most teens cannot fall asleep.

invented.quote: A student who has to catch a bus before 7 a.m. is working against their own biology.
invented.why: The brief does not state what time students catch the bus.

invented.quote: That is why the American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that high schools start no earlier than 8:30.
invented.why: The brief states the AAP recommendation, but does not give the biological reason why the AAP makes that recommendation.

invented.quote: It is linked to weaker concentration and memory, more anxiety and depression, and more car crashes among young drivers.

invented.quote: Every morning I send tired students back to class after an ice pack or a few minutes' rest, knowing that what they really need is sleep.
